deck_context.source_summary: V3 manuscript studies within-field reconstruction from sparse log-permeability observations on three independent GSTools Gaussian synthetic fields, each with three observation/initialization repeats. A dual-network Darcy PINN predicts log-permeability and auxiliary pressure, using real PDE and boundary residual losses. A PennyLane differentiable parameterized quantum circuit simulated by exact state vectors replaces only the classical Tanh permeability feature block. The experiment crosses C/Q representation with RBA and MC training enhancements and evaluates held-out k-space relative L2 error, independent equation residual, auxiliary pressure, downstream coarse-grid FVM flux, and training time.
deck_context.core_claim: Q improves mean held-out permeability relative L2 error from 0.337094 to 0.306759 (9.00%) versus C at fixed epochs, but not every field/run. RBA greatly reduces independent PDE residual but scarcely improves k error; MC alone does not improve primary error and costs time. Downstream flux and simulation time do not follow k-error ranking.
canonical_terms: 参数化量子线路的精确模拟
deck_context.scientific_boundaries: This is a differentiable quantum circuit simulated on a classical CPU, not a sine-based quantum-inspired phase network or real quantum hardware. The actual V3 training includes Darcy strong-form and no-flow boundary losses, but no internal pressure labels. The only supervised observations are sparse log-permeability. No V2 residual spatial correction, known-point backfilling or full-field calibration. Three synthetic fields and nine fits per method are not nine independent fields. No generalization to unseen fields, field measurements, quantum speedup, hardware advantage or universal superiority. Numerical plots must not invent training traces, error bars, or field measurements.
